curiosityReview.honestPremise: How did nuclear reactors operate on Earth about two billion years ago, without anyone building them?
curiosityReview.coldAudienceReason: A nuclear reactor seems to require deliberate engineering. Real rock deposits sustaining that process before humans existed demand more than the label natural radioactivity as an answer.
curiosityReview.storyRoute: Establish the reactor-before-builders premise; introduce anomalous uranium and fission-product evidence; reconstruct the ancient fuel and water conditions; explain the inferred heat/water feedback; resolve how a natural system could do part of what we associate with engineered reactors. Keep established occurrence distinct from reconstructed operation.

truthBoundary.rationale: Natural self-sustaining fission is supported by inspected sources; no ancient engineered plant, electricity production, explosion or lost-civilization assertion. Water-cycle interpretation must be qualified.

opportunityJudgment.rationale: The premise is independently compelling before any graphics; the answer transforms nuclear reaction from an exclusively human-created process into a conditional physical one. Mechanism and isotope detective work give multiple earned steps beyond a one-line fact.

rationale: Magnivis selects Oklo because the unadorned premise challenges an everyday belief about nuclear reactors, and its payoff explains the physical conditions that could replace engineering rather than stopping at nature did it. Smalls supplies stronger human stakes and majority cycling a rigorous conceptual puzzle; both were assessed on their own merits. For this slot, Oklo combines immediate curiosity, a reconstructable evidence trail and layered causal understanding most strongly. Neither recent physics approval, calibration resemblance/distance nor available rendering tools determined the choice. This is accountable editorial judgment, not predicted performance.

premiseAssessment.truthfulFraming: Natural uranium deposits in present-day Gabon sustained nuclear fission about two billion years ago. Reactors refers to natural reaction zones producing heat, not human-built generating stations. Occurrence is established preliminarily; groundwater-driven cycling is an evidence-based reconstruction with scope limits.
caveats: No electricity-generating power station, lost civilization, bomb or operating reactor today implied.
Exact cycle timings are inferred for one studied reaction zone, not all Oklo zones or a directly measured ancient clock.
Final claim-level evidence review and wording remain pending; primary2004 paper body not accessed.
Conflicting operating-duration figure excluded; precise durations, temperatures, zone counts and isotope percentages are not needed for the intended premise.
materialRisks: The planned explanatory reward includes inferred groundwater feedback; development must preserve that distinction and make neutron moderation intelligible without overstating reconstruction. A material failure or change of payoff returns to selection/Premise Review.
